# seakarr

Automated Soulseek music downloader with library quality upgrading.

## Features

- **Library quality scanner** — walks your music library directories, reads audio tags (FLAC, MP3, AAC,
  OGG, Opus, WAV, WMA, and more via [lofty](https://crates.io/crates/lofty)), and identifies albums
  whose tracks are in a format outside `filters.allowed_extensions` or fall below the
  configurable bitrate threshold.
- **Upgrade mode** — for each album needing an upgrade, searches the Soulseek network, ranks
  candidates by advertised speed (adjusted by measured-throughput reputation), free-slot bonus, bitrate bonus,
  album-name match and peer reliability, and downloads the best match. The result is written into your
  library when the artist already has a folder under a configured `library.paths` entry, and stays in
  `storage.staging_dir` when it does not; an album selected by `library_upgrade.enabled` is replaced in
  place. An upgrade whose every destination already holds a strictly better file
  keeps those files and still completes the album, so the staging copy is removed without a new file being
  written. A candidate whose files omit the bitrate attribute scores zero on the bitrate bonus once
  `filters.min_bit_rate` is set, so a peer that reports one is preferred; it is still admitted, because its
  real quality is verified after download.
- **Discover mode** — derives the artist list from your library (tags first,
  folder names as the fallback), keeps only the artists that own a folder of
  their own, asks MusicBrainz which conceptual albums each of those is missing,
  and downloads only those. An artist the library only knows as a guest inside
  another artist's folder is skipped, and the run summary reports how many were
  skipped that way; name one explicitly with `--artist` to process it anyway.
  Albums already present are never
  searched or re-downloaded, and each run stops after
  `discover.max_cycle_downloads` download attempts so a large library fills in
  over successive runs. Release types come from `discography.allowed_types`.
- **Manual & batch modes** — search for a specific artist/album on demand, or process a newline-separated
  text file of `artist - album` lines to download a curated wantlist.
  A run places each completed album into the artist's existing library folder when one exists
  anywhere under a configured `library.paths` entry; when the artist has no folder there, or the
  album's destination folder already exists, a manual run keeps the download in
  `storage.staging_dir` (batch and upgrade runs merge into the existing folder instead, keeping
  any file that already parses as audio). An
  album-only request names no artist, so it always stays in staging and says nothing: only manual
  mode can express one, because upgrade mode rejects `--album` on its own and a batch line is trimmed
  before it is parsed, so a line written as `" - Album"` is read as an artist-only line. An artist-naming run with a configured library path explains a
  staging-only download once it has one.
- **Authoritative artist discography** — artist-only manual runs resolve conceptual albums from MusicBrainz
  release groups (cached locally for 30 days) and then run one sequential `Artist Album` Soulseek search per
  eligible album, oldest first. The same authoritative resolution powers `discover` mode for every artist
  it sweeps — those that own a folder named after them. Release categories and optional MusicBrainz artist IDs are configurable; the
  previous folder heuristic remains the explicit opt-out and the visible fallback.
- **Quality filtering** — filter Soulseek results by file extension, minimum
  bitrate, excluded keywords, and upload availability. With
  `download.max_queue_length: 0` a peer must offer a free upload slot; a
  positive limit also admits zero-slot peers until their reported queue
  position can be validated. Path-traversal names are rejected.
- **Peer reputation** — remembers each peer's effective throughput (bytes ÷ transfer time: retry delays plus
  the final transfer, excluding queue wait) and success rate (in SQLite), and ranks search results by a blend
  of advertised and measured throughput plus a reliability factor, so fast, reliable peers are preferred and
  slow or error-prone peers are demoted — regardless of what you search for. Controlled by
  `search.peer_reputation` (default `true`).
- **Download resilience** — speed monitoring with configurable minimums (a peer
  whose smoothed speed is below `min_upload_speed_kbps` past
  `speed_check_wait_secs` is cancelled and treated as a failed candidate rather

=== ownership rule in the design doc ===
### The destination is the artist's own library folder

A placed album lands beside the artist's existing albums, under the directory
the scanner found those albums in. Genre nesting is preserved and no second
artist tree is created. `library.paths[0]` is deliberately not used as the
destination root: for a nested library it is a genre or user directory, so
albums would be written outside the artist's own tree.

### The destination pair comes from the scan, and the on-disk folder name wins

The scanner already derives, per album, the directory *above* the artist folder
(`ScannedAlbum::path`). The index additionally records the on-disk name of the
artist folder itself, so a destination is a pair of (root, artist directory).

The artist directory that is actually on disk — not the tag-derived query
spelling — is used for the `%artist%` component. Tag spellings and folder
spellings differ in real libraries (`Guns 'n' Roses` in tags, `Guns N Roses` on
disk); expanding the pattern with the tag spelling would create a second artist
directory beside the existing one. MusicBrainz queries and processed-album
records keep using the tag-preferred query spelling, which is unchanged
behaviour.

Where one artist's albums were found under more than one root, the destination
with the most albums wins, ties broken alphabetically. This mirrors the rule the
index already uses to choose a query spelling, and keeps the destination
independent of filesystem walk order.

Both prerequisites preserved. Investigation complete — I reproduced the failure end-to-end, including against the real library subtree.

## Phase 1 — Root Cause Investigation

### The error surface and the data flow

```text
main.rs:580            runner::run_discover_mode(client, config, db, artist, ...)
runner.rs:2436         scan_library_cancellable(config, ...)        -> Vec<ScannedAlbum>
runner.rs:2442         discover::build_index(&scanned)              -> LibraryIndex
runner.rs:2444         discover::select_artists(&index, &excludes, artist_filter)
discover.rs:501        if filter_key.is_none() || !index.has_artist(name) {
discover.rs:502-504        return Err(SeakarrError::Config("artist {name:?} was not found ..."))
```

`LibraryIndex.artists` is populated **only** by `build_index(albums)` (discover.rs:384), iterating `ScannedAlbum`s. `scan_library` emits a `ScannedAlbum` only for a recognised audio file whose relative path yields an album component (`discs::album_index`, else `len - 2 >= 1`, scanner.rs:392-397). **An artist folder with no audio file beneath it contributes nothing to the index, so it is not an artist as far as discover mode is concerned.**

### Reproduction — synthetic fixtures and the real library

Repro crate at `/tmp/seakarr-repro` (path-dep on the repo, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/seakarr/target`, nothing in the repo touched):

| Shape (root → artist folder) | `scan_library` result | `has_artist("shy fx")` | `select_artists(Some("shy fx"))` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** root=genre dir, `Shy Fx/` **empty** | 1 album, none from Shy Fx | `false` | `Err(configuration error: artist "shy fx" was not found in the library; discover mode can only narrow to artists already present)` |
| **B** root=genre dir, `Shy Fx/01 - loose track.flac` | 1 album, loose file **dropped** | `false` | same `Err` |
| **C** root=genre's parent, `Drum And Bass/Shy Fx/01 - loose track.flac` | 2 albums; **`artist="Drum And Bass" album="Shy Fx"`** | `false` | same `Err` |
| **D** root=genre dir, `Shy Fx/Some Album/folder.jpg` only | 1 album, none from Shy Fx | `false` | same `Err` |

Real library, `/media/Music/Paul/Albums/Dance/Drum And Bass` (read-only):

```text
scanned albums       = 196          <- matches the user's log line exactly
LibraryIndex artists = 92
direct child folders = 29;  folders that produced an album = 28
folders with NO album scanned (1) = ["Shy Fx"]
has_artist("shy fx") = false        (also false for "Shy Fx")
select_artists(Some("shy fx")) = Err(configuration error: artist "shy fx" was not found ...)
ArtistFolderIndex::find("shy fx")  = Some(("/media/Music/Paul/Albums/Dance/Drum And Bass", "Shy Fx"))
```

**This is the reported failure, reproduced deterministically** — 196 albums matches the user's log, and the error text matches verbatim (the log paste drops the `{name:?}` quotes).

### The user's hypothesis — half right, and now separable

- For a **genuinely empty** folder (the reported case) or an artwork-only one, **no mis-keying happens**: the folder is simply *invisible*. "No subfolders underneath" is not the trigger — **"no audio file beneath it that lands in an album component"** is.
- The described mechanism **is** real, but needs loose audio files *directly* in the artist folder **and** a root at least two levels above it: shape **C** produced a phantom `artist="Drum And Bass"` (the genre!) with `album="Shy Fx"`. With the root at the artist's parent — the CLI case — those loose files are dropped entirely by the minimum-depth rule instead. So the same "artist folder with no albums" produces *two different* wrong outcomes depending on root depth.

### Why the artist is invisible rather than explained

- The sweep silently omits it: it is absent from `artist_keys`, so it lands in neither `artists` nor `no_folder` — the run summary under-reports instead of naming it. `owns_folder` reads album-derived `artist_folders`, so the `no_folder` gate is blind for the same reason.
- **Relaxing the gate alone would not be enough.** `select_artists` then calls `index.artist_destination(key)`, which returns `None` for an artist with no index entry (discover.rs:203-218) — the code warns `"artist {key:?} has albums but no destination; skipping"` and `continue`s. A folder-only artist needs a destination too.

### The information the fix needs already exists, in the same module

`ArtistFolderIndex` (added v0.27.0) walks the configured roots for **directory names only** and resolved `shy fx` → `Some((parent, "Shy Fx"))` in every shape above, including with zero audio files. `runner::automatic_place_target` already converts exactly that into `LibraryTarget::Place { root, artist_dir }` for manual/batch/batch-placement. **Discover is the only mode that derives its artist list from albums alone.**

### Change history — not a regression

Both the gate and `build_index` date to the discover-mode commit `dc3a9b5` (2026-09-15); nothing since touched the behaviour (v0.29.0 changed only comments in `discover.rs`). Two design docs already record adjacent **accepted costs**: the gap-filling design's *"Artist source: tag artist with folder fallback"* (2026-09-18 amendment — 509 tag-derived artists resolved to 49 album artists, hence the ownership gate) and the placement design's *Deliberate limits* bullet *"a pattern that omits `%album%` … an artist whose albums are all written flat has no index entry and disappears from the work list"*, which also states `has_artist`/`artist_keys` **deliberately** ignore the folder alias. **The reported case — a folder with no albums at all — is not among those documented limits; it is an unhandled gap.**

Environment note: the container-vs-bare-metal path difference is not a factor — reproducing against `/media/Music/...` yields the same 196 albums and the same error.

### Decisions needed before a fix

The fix defines *what counts as an artist folder*, which extends discover's artist derivation and changes a public function's inputs — so it needs the user's call rather than mine (AGENTS.md rule 5).

Checked before answering, and it changes the practical detail: **discover does consult the processed-albums DB** (`fill_artist_gap` → `process_album` → `skip_already_processed`, runner.rs:502, 2347), so a staging download is recorded and won't be re-fetched each cycle.

## Thoughts on your proposal

**I agree with the core of it** — dropping the hard exit for an artist the library genuinely doesn't know is the right call, and it matches behaviour that already exists elsewhere: manual/batch resolve placement via `automatic_place_target`, which falls back to `LibraryTarget::StagingOnly` and explains the outcome through `explain_staging_outcome`. Today `--artist <unknown>` in discover mode is the only place that refuses to work at all.

**But I'd push back on applying staging to the case you actually hit**, for three reasons:

1. **The evidence is there, and staging throws it away.** We verified `ArtistFolderIndex::find("shy fx") = Some(("/media/Music/Paul/Albums/Dance/Drum And Bass", "Shy Fx"))` — the folder exists and the placement machinery already turns exactly that pair into `LibraryTarget::Place` for manual/batch (runner.rs:1683-1692). Downloads would land in `.../Drum And Bass/Shy Fx/<album>/`, the folder you created, with **no new inference rule** (it's a name-keyed lookup, so no phantom-artist risk). Sending this case to staging instead leaves your folder empty and makes you file it by hand — which defers the "identify album-less artist folders" problem rather than solving it.

2. **Processed-record wrinkle.** Staging downloads *are* recorded as processed, so they aren't re-downloaded every cycle (good). But that cuts the other way later: once the folder exists and you want them filed, a later run will skip them as already processed unless you pass `--ignore-processed`. Worth accepting knowingly, since it's a step the operator has to remember.

3. **It removes a real typo guard.** `--artist` with an unknown name currently fails loudly, and that's pinned by a test (`an_unknown_filter_artist_is_a_configuration_error`, discover.rs:2036). Phase 1 complete — root cause identified, reproduced, and the behaviour contract agreed. No code changed (`git status` clean, HEAD `a47bdc6`); repro lives in `/tmp/seakarr-repro` (regenerates its fixtures on each run).

## Root cause

**`discover::select_artists` validates `--artist` against an artist list that is built only from scanned albums.** `LibraryIndex.artists` is populated by `build_index(albums)` (discover.rs:384), and `scan_library` emits a `ScannedAlbum` only when a recognised audio file's relative path yields an album component (scanner.rs:392-397). An artist folder holding no audio therefore produces **no entry at all**, so `index.has_artist("shy fx")` is `false` and discover.rs:501-504 returns the hard `SeakarrError::Config` you saw. The same artist is also absent from `artist_keys`, so the sweep silently omits it and it lands in neither `artists` nor `no_folder` — invisible rather than reported. Both the gate and `build_index` date to the original discover commit `dc3a9b5` (2026-09-15): this is an unhandled gap in the design, not a regression.

Reproduced on the real subtree (`/media/Music/Paul/Albums/Dance/Drum And Bass`, read-only): **196 albums** — matching your log line exactly — 29 child folders, 28 produced an album, **only `Shy Fx` produced none**, `has_artist("shy fx") = false`, and the error text matches verbatim.

## Your hypothesis, precisely

- A genuinely empty (or artwork-only) folder is **not mis-keyed** — it is simply invisible. "No subfolders" isn't the trigger; **"no audio file beneath it"** is.
- The mis-keying you described is real but needs loose audio files *directly* in the artist folder **and** a library root ≥2 levels above: that shape produced a phantom `artist="Drum And Bass"` with `album="Shy Fx"`. With the root at the artist's parent (your CLI case) those loose files are dropped by the minimum-depth rule instead. So "artist folder with no albums" has **two** wrong outcomes depending on root depth.

## Agreed behaviour contract

1. **`--artist <name>`**: album-derived artist → unchanged. Else, if the name resolves to an existing library folder (`ArtistFolderIndex`, directory-name walk) → treat as a real artist, fetch the discography, and **place into that folder** (`LibraryTarget::Place { root: parent, artist_dir: "Shy Fx", skip_existing_album: false }`). Else (no folder, no albums) → **warn and keep downloads in staging** (`LibraryTarget::StagingOnly`) instead of exiting.
2. **Unfiltered sweep**: unchanged — album-derived only, so an album-less folder is never swept automatically (and, per this choice, not reported in the summary either).

Verified supporting facts: `ArtistFolderIndex::find("shy fx")` already returns `Some((".../Drum And Bass", "Shy Fx"))` with zero audio files, and `automatic_place_target` already converts exactly that pair into a `Place` target — the machinery exists and is used by manual/batch; discover is the only mode that never consults it. `--library-path` **replaces** `config.library.paths` (config.rs:775-777), so the folder walk will see the CLI root. Staging downloads are recorded as processed (`skip_already_processed`, runner.rs:502), so they won't be re-fetched each cycle — but a later run will also skip them unless `--ignore-processed`.

## Constraints the TDD step must handle

- **A destination is required, and `LibraryIndex` cannot supply one**: `artist_destination` returns `None` for a folder-only artist, so relaxing the gate alone would hit the `"artist {key:?} has albums but no destination; skipping"` guard and drop it. The `(parent, artist_dir)` pair must come from the folder walk.
- **Keep `select_artists` pure**: it is a pure function over `LibraryIndex`, and two unit tests encode the current contract — `an_unknown_filter_artist_is_a_configuration_error` (discover.rs:2036) and `a_folder_only_spelling_cannot_be_selected_with_a_filter` (discover.rs:1441). Both must be **re-pinned deliberately**; resolving the folder in the runner (which already builds an `ArtistFolderIndex`) and passing the result in keeps those fixtures meaningful and avoids giving `select_artists` a filesystem dependency.
- **Docs and spec are now contradicted**: README's discover paragraph, the placement design's *Deliberate limits* bullet (which states `has_artist`/`artist_keys` *deliberately* ignore the folder alias and such an artist "cannot be named with `--artist`"), and the gap-filling design's *`--artist` is an optional narrowing filter* section. Repo convention expects a spec + plan pair under `docs/agent/`.
- **Open residual risk, not covered by your two decisions**: the loose-track mis-keying (shapes B/C) stays as-is, and shape C still produces a phantom genre-artist entry in the sweep. Also, a loose file is invisible to presence, so its album is re-selected and re-downloaded (placement never overwrites existing audio). Flagging it as a separate follow-up rather than silently bundling it.

## Behaviour implemented (the agreed contract)

- `--artist <name>` where the library has **no album** for the artist now resolves `<name>` against the library's folders: found → work item with `ArtistDestination::Folder { parent, on-disk name }`, and the album is **placed into the folder the operator created**; not found → work item with `ArtistDestination::Staging`, the run **warns** and continues instead of exiting.
- The **sweep is unchanged** (album-derived), and folder evidence is consulted *only* for an explicit name.
- A **blank** `--artist` remains a configuration error (unchanged, still pinned).

## TDD cycles — every test watched failing first

| Test | RED evidence (observed) | GREEN |
|---|---|---|
| `an_explicitly_named_artist_that_only_owns_a_folder_is_selected` (new, discover.rs) | First `E0061: this function takes 3 arguments but 4 were supplied` + `E0560: no field named destination` + `E0433: cannot find type ArtistDestination` (feature absent); after type scaffolding, assertion-level: `Err(Config("artist \"blockhead\" was not found in the library…"))` | folder branch added |

| `discover_fills_an_artist_that_owns_a_folder_with_no_albums` (runner, replaces `discover_rejects_a_filter_artist_absent_from_the_library`) | panicked **"the album must be placed inside the artist folder the operator created"** — the album went to staging: the reported symptom | runner wired to resolve folder evidence |

### `discover`

Controls `discover` mode, which fills gaps in your library for artists you
already have.

Gap filling follows folders, not tags. An artist is only swept when at least one
of its albums was found in a folder named after the artist itself, so an album
tagged `ARTIST=Apashe` that sits inside the `Bassnectar` folder does not make
Apashe an artist discover fills: it is skipped, counted in the run summary as

log. Name such an artist with `--artist` to process it anyway. Naming an artist
explicitly does not require the library to hold an album for it: a folder named
after it becomes the destination for its downloads, and naming an artist with
neither an album nor a folder warns and keeps the downloads in staging. The accepted cost
is that an artist whose albums live in a folder with a different name — beyond
case, spacing, or width folding, which the gate tolerates — or in a
folder whose name sanitisation rewrote, is no longer swept automatically.

4. **unfiltered sweep unchanged** — `src/runner.rs:2448-2454` skips the `find` call when `artist_filter = None`, so `filter_folder = None`. `src/discover.rs:580-628` only enters the early-return branches when `filter = Some(...)`, so the main loop processes `index.artist_keys()` exactly as before. Pre-existing tests like `discover_does_not_gap_fill_an_artist_filed_only_inside_another_artists_folder` (`src/runner.rs:5907`) and `a_folder_owner_keeps_being_gap_filled_while_its_guest_artist_does_not` (`src/discover.rs:2005`) still apply.

5. **blank `--artist` is a config error** — `src/discover.rs:527-532` returns `SeakarrError::Config` when `filter_key.is_none()`. The `discover` CLI also rejects blank `--artist` earlier (`src/mode.rs:253-258`), so the defense in depth works through both paths. Verified by unit test `a_blank_filter_artist_is_a_configuration_error` (`src/discover.rs:2183-2188`).

### Findings

- **P1, README.md:1112-1116, stale user-facing FAQ:** The Q&A "How do I fill in missing albums for one artist only?" still asserts `"The name must already exist in your library; discover derives the artist list from your library and never adds an artist you do not have."` This is now false: `--mode discover --artist "Name"` selects an artist the album-derived index does not hold when a folder of that name exists, and warns + keeps in staging when neither an album nor a folder exists. Failure mode: an operator reading the README will be afraid to try the documented (in other README sections and in the spec) workflow that the diff now supports. The diff updates other parts of the file but leaves this paragraph untouched. The fix: rewrite the paragraph to describe the new behavior — folder as destination when the name has no album, warning + staging when neither.

- **P1, README.md:1147-1151, misleading user-facing description:** The note `"--artist` narrowing still keys on the tag spelling, and the artist work list now also requires the artist to own a folder of its own, so a name spelled differently on disk than in its tags is skipped by the sweep and has to be named with `--artist`"` is misleading after the diff. After the change, `--artist` can resolve against the folder spelling even when the typed name matches no tag spelling; the "workaround" the paragraph describes is now built into the mechanism. Failure mode: an operator whose on-disk folder spelling differs from the tag spelling will be told `--artist` only keys on the tag spelling and assume they must instead rename the folder, when in fact they should just run with `--artist "<folder-spelling>"`. The fix: revise the note to acknowledge that `--artist` resolves against both the album-derived index and the folder walk, and that the on-disk spelling wins when the tag spelling is absent.

- **P2, src/main.rs:92, stale CLI help:** The doc comment for `--artist` reads `"Artist for manual mode; in discover mode a narrowing filter that also overrides discover.exclude_artists and the folder-ownership gate"`. It does not mention the new behavior (naming an artist not in the library works). Failure mode: a user running `seakarr --help` won't learn that they can name an artist that has no album yet. The fix: extend the comment with one clause matching the README table row at README.md:202.

- **P2, src/discover.rs:712 discover_notices(), run summary gap:** The new "kept in staging due to no folder" condition is reported only as `tracing::warn!` in the log. `discover_notices` (lines 712-781) emits nothing for this case. The run summary therefore shows `"Downloaded (1): Nobody — Missing (1 tracks) -> /tmp/.../Nobody--Missing (kept in staging)"` with no explanation; an operator reading only the summary cannot tell whether the staging is a bug or the new design. The fix: add a counter (e.g. `DiscoverCounters::staged_no_folder: usize`) and a corresponding notice in `discover_notices`, mirroring the existing `no_folder` notice for the automatic sweep.

- **P2, docs/agent/specs/2026-09-15-musicbrainz-library-gap-filling-design.md:285-287, awkward supersession:** The paragraph above still reads `"The name must exist in the library index, otherwise the run fails with a configuration error naming the artist; a typo can never silently do nothing."` The supersession note at lines 296-307 directly contradicts this in the next paragraph. Failure mode: the spec reads as internally inconsistent on a casual read. The fix: rephrase or relocate the old sentence (e.g. remove it, mark it struck-through, or move it under a "previously, before Superseded notes" subhead).

- **P2, src/discover.rs:1899 test-name imprecision:** The new unit test `an_explicitly_named_artist_that_only_owns_a_folder_is_selected` uses the fixture `scanned_at("Aesop Rock", "Appetite", "/library", "Blockhead")`. The Blockhead folder contains an Aesop Rock album — the artist Blockhead does not "only own a folder"; the folder is occupied by another artist's albums. Failure mode: a reader who skims test names will get the wrong mental model. The fix: rename to something like `an_explicitly_named_folder_name_selects_that_folder_even_when_unrelated_albums_live_in_it`, or move Aesop Rock's album out so the folder is empty (but that would not exercise the realistic case).

### Merge verdict

**OK with notes.** Code correctness is solid; the contract under review is satisfied and the two new integration tests cover both the "folder exists" and "no folder no album" branches end-to-end. The mechanical `as_chunks::<3>().0.iter()` fix in `src/main.rs:1188-1196,1231-1238` is correct (same behavior as the prior `chunks_exact(3)`, just clippy-clean). Documentation needs follow-up before the next release so users aren't told the opposite of what the code does, but no documentation bug prevents the feature from working today.

### Residual risks

- **Behavioral surprise in mixed-tag/folder layouts.** A library that holds Aesop Rock albums in a `Blockhead/` folder and an explicit `--artist "Blockhead"` run will fetch the discography of the MusicBrainz artist named "Blockhead" (a different artist), not Aesop Rock's missing albums. The diff is consistent with the spec, but operators with type-tag/spelled-differently libraries may be surprised. The doc updates called out above are the mitigation.

- **Coverage gap.** No integration test exercises `find` returning `Some` for a name that resolves to a folder containing an unrelated artist's albums (the unit test does, via direct call to `select_artists`, but `run_discover_mode_with_provider` is not tested with the Aesop-Rock-in-Blockhead-folder shape). A small additional `#[tokio::test]` would catch any future regression in the wiring between `ArtistFolderIndex::find` and `select_artists`.

- **Test runs not executed.** As instructed, I did not run `cargo test`. The two new integration tests in `src/runner.rs` and the new unit tests in `src/discover.rs` need a clean `cargo test` run; the analysis above verifies the logic against the code but cannot prove the Rust compiles. The clippy-fix in `src/main.rs` is a mechanical substitution and is low-risk; the new `&Path`/`&str` lifetime in `select_artists`'s `filter_folder: Option<(&Path, &str)>` is borrowed from a local `Option<(PathBuf, String)>` whose `as_ref().map(...)` produces values that outlive the call, so I see no compile-time issue, but the supervisor must run `cargo test` to confirm.

Run `--mode discover --artist "Artist Name"`. Naming an artist the library holds
an album for narrows the sweep to that artist and also bypasses the
folder-ownership gate, which is how you reach an artist whose albums sit in a
folder named after somebody else. The name need not exist in the library yet:
when a folder named after the artist exists, the artist is processed and its
albums are placed into that folder, and when there is neither an album nor a
folder the run warns and keeps the downloads in staging. To fetch a specific
album instead, use
`--mode manual --artist "Artist Name" --album "Album Title"`.

## Reporting contract

Notices emitted by a discover run, in this order when present:

- `discover: no eligible library artists found; nothing to do`
- `discover: <N> album(s) already present; skipped`
- `discover: excluded <N> artist(s) by discover.exclude_artists`
- `discover: <N> artist(s) skipped: no folder of their own`
- `discover: <N> artist(s) skipped from cached resolution failures`
- `discover: <N> artist(s) unresolved on MusicBrainz: <name>, ...` (first ten

- `discover: <N> artist(s) had no albums matching discography.allowed_types`
- `discover: provider failed for <name> (<reason>); artist skipped`
- `discover: download budget of <N> reached at artist "<name>"; <X> of <Y>
  artist(s) examined`

Artist-only manual runs additionally emit:

- `Artist-only run: <N> album(s) already present; skipped`
- `Artist-only run: all <N> eligible album(s) already present`

The selector can only narrow the library-derived list, never add to it; fetching
a discography for an artist who is not in the library remains artist-only manual
mode's job. It can, however, reach an artist the automatic sweep skips, because
naming an artist explicitly overrides the folder-ownership gate (and
`exclude_artists`). `search.manual.artist` is not consulted by discover,
consistent with
mode resolution already ignoring inactive configuration values.

=== [F6] spec note 297-312 ===

**Superseded on 2026-10-05: the selector is no longer limited to artists the
index holds, and an absent name is no longer a configuration error.** The
reported failure was an operator who had created `<artist>/` before any album of
that artist existed in it; discover refused to run, because the artist list is
album-derived. `--mode discover --artist "Name"` now resolves the name against
the library's folders when the album-derived index does not hold it: a folder
named after the artist makes it a work item, with that folder as the destination
and its on-disk spelling as the MusicBrainz query, because there is no artist tag
to prefer. A name the library holds neither an album nor a folder for warns and
keeps its downloads in staging rather than ending the run. A blank name remains
a configuration error. The automatic sweep is unchanged: folder evidence is
consulted only for an explicitly named artist, so a folder the operator never
named is never gap-filled.

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/discover.rs` | 423 (`ArtistDestination`, `select_artists`' folder-evidence argument, trimmed staged name, outcome-based `staged_albums` counter and notice, tests) |
| `src/runner.rs` | 199 (lazy folder resolution for the named artist, `Place`/`StagingOnly` dispatch from the destination, outcome counting, end-to-end tests) |
| `src/main.rs` | 17 (`--artist` CLI help; two pre-existing `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint fixes in test code) |
| `README.md` | 55 (discover bullet, `--artist` row, `discover` section, behaviour narrative, FAQ) |

| `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` | `0.29.0` → `0.30.0` (MINOR: new functionality plus a public-API change on a pre-1.0 crate) |
| **Total** | **8 files, +644 / −104** |

**What shipped:** `--mode discover --artist "shy fx"` no longer exits with `artist ... was not found in the library`. A named artist the album-derived index does not hold is resolved against the library's folders — the folder becomes the work item's destination and its on-disk spelling is what MusicBrainz and the search are asked about; with neither an album nor a folder the run warns and keeps downloads in staging. The automatic sweep is unchanged, a blank name is still a configuration error, and the summary reports only albums genuinely kept in staging.

**Verification behind the release:** tests re-run on the bumped tree → **1231 passed, 0 failed**; the QA gate on the same tree was `CLEAN` (clippy 0, fmt 0, coverage 97.40% lines, `cargo audit`/`cargo deny` clean, markdownlint 0, pre-commit 4/4).

**Cleanup:** none applicable — Option 1 preserves the branch, the repo is not a worktree (`GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`), the tree is clean and `main` is in sync with `origin/main` at `171f65c`. Branch `main` preserved locally and remotely; `--delete-branch` was not used. Three pre-existing `pi-subagents/*` scratch worktrees under `/data/worktrees/seakarr/` are harness-owned (not created for this task and not under the repo's `.worktrees/`), so they were left untouched.

⚠️ **One caveat reported rather than smoothed over:** the code-review loop reached its **3-round cap**, so it emitted `COMPLETE` rather than `CLEAN`. Round 3's three fixes (folder-scoped presence rule pinned and documented, outcome-based staging count, three corrected README sentences) were applied and passed every QA gate, but no reviewer round remained to re-verify them — manual review of those three is still recommended.
